payload.name: Preserve Explicit Activity Formats in Enrichment
payload.description: When a message describes a hobby or activity with emotional significance and explicitly names concrete formats, outlets, or instances (e.g., journal, blog post), during extraction or enrichment.
content: During extraction, when a message ties an activity to a general feeling (e.g., 'writing is my rock') and explicitly names concrete forms or outlets (e.g., a journal, an online blog post), capture each named form as a distinct facet in the profile/preference/event memory; do not collapse the candidate into only the emotional significance.
When enriching an existing memory about the activity, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly named concrete forms rather than replacing the memory with a narrower paraphrase.

Before SKIPping a candidate that mentions a specific instance (e.g., a blog post) because a related general memory exists, verify that the specific fact is already present; if not, add or merge it. Stop after capturing only the explicitly named forms; do not infer unstated ones.

solves: Extraction often keeps only the emotional summary of an activity and drops explicitly named concrete forms (e.g., journal, blog post), so later questions about what the person actually does are unanswerable.
